steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Audience Complicity: Dramatic irony makes the audience feel involved - we know secrets, we anticipate outcomes, we're emotionally invested. | Why Off-Stage?: Some violence too extreme for stage; imagination more powerful; focuses on psychological aftermath rather than physical act. | Banquo as Foil: He shows what Macbeth could have been - the alternative path. His murder marks Macbeth's descent into true tyranny. | Dramatic Techniques Strategy: Focus on what the AUDIENCE experiences. Ask: "What does the audience know that characters don't? What can the audience see that characters can't? How does Shakespeare control what we feel and when?" Analyse dramatic irony, soliloquies, entrances/exits, and on-stage vs off-stage action. Always link technique to audience effect.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is dramatic irony and give an example from "Macbeth". | How does Shakespeare use the supernatural to create tension? | What is the function of Banquo as a foil to Macbeth?
